findings_addressed.oracle: Gate Part A (unconditional): an httpx.MockTransport stub is injected at the HTTP-transport boundary; OllamaProvider.connect() + list_models() run with full production parsing logic (_fetch_local_models, _populate_ollama_models, _fetch_model_metadata, _query_model_show). Assertions verify: exactly 2 records returned, ids prefixed 'local/', provider==ProviderName.OLLAMA, llama3 context_window==8192 (parsed from stub /api/show 'num_ctx 8192'), llava supports_tools==True (template '{{ .Tools }}' detected), llava supports_vision==True ('llava' in name). Gate Part B (conditional): live provider gates remain for any configured provider, but the test no longer skips when configured_count==0 — Gate Part A always runs.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: Change id_prefix="local/" to id_prefix="" inside OllamaProvider._populate_ollama_models() in src/intellicrack/providers/ollama.py. The assertion 'stub_ids == {"local/llama3", "local/llava"}' turns red because the returned ids would be {"llama3", "llava"}. This is a one-line change to production code that definitively falsifies the gate.
findings_addressed.anti_pattern_eliminated: N3 (skip masking real capability) — the original test unconditionally called pytest.skip() when configured_count==0, which is the common case in CI/sandbox environments. The test now always exercises real OllamaProvider parsing code through the stub transport path regardless of whether any live provider credentials are present.

notes: Re-hardened in response to adversarial reviewer finding that configured_count==0 still caused unconditional skip. The fix introduces an always-running Gate Part A that exercises OllamaProvider end-to-end with a fake httpx.MockTransport injected only at the network-transport boundary (the only legitimate mock point). The stub serves /api/tags with two known model records and /api/show responses with precise metadata, allowing the full _populate_ollama_models + _query_model_show parsing pipeline to be validated without any live endpoint. Gate Part B (live providers) runs only when credentials are present but no longer causes a skip when they are absent — the test always produces a meaningful signal.
